content:
Trying to get back into the game - combat alternates between bashing peasants and instant death
"Fight Bernard" "Get stats" "Henry isn't meant to be good"

My strength is maxed, my defence is maxed, 15 warfare, 15 mace and Bernard calls me daddy. He doesn't come close to landing a blow on me with any weapon. 

I beat interlopers without issue. Slaughtered them like cattle. On my way fast travelling back I was stopped by 3 peasants who, in spite of my armour being the best I can find, nearly killed me. Every attack was countered, my ripostes were countered, it was just a joke. The peasants were more of an issue. 

Going back to Skalitz for some hidden loot quest, there's 5 bandits there. In spite of having beaten interlopers, they're countering me every attack or stunlocking me. I beat them once, then had the game crash to desktop not long after that. "Not saving is a good mechanic" or something, right? 

So I went back, decided I barely won last time, let's do it on a horse and just shoot them. I get 2 arrows off, I kill one, my horse clips through the ground and I think it died? Not sure. 

Anyway, I'm unseated, there's 4 left. I get 2 down to half health with this clunky-ass targeting system, suddenly I'm stunlocked and dead. I have stamina, I press block when the green shield appears, doesn't matter get hit anyway. 

There's this fundamental disconnect for me. If I can beat Bernard without him even scratching me, playing both aggressively and countering, surely I understand how to block. If I can beat interlopers, obviously I can handle multiple people. But 3 peasants nearly killed me immedately after because every attack was blocked, every counter was countered. And now these guys are just the worst and I feel frankly stuck. 

The advice I can find is "lol git gud" "don't fight things" "it should be hard". Yeah great, but none of that is advice. My stats are fine, if not perfect. I obviously get the gameplay to an extent, so saying "fight Bernard" isn't going to help. 

Feinting doesn't help. Riposte is worthless, and I've never seen this master strike people mention using a mace. Clinching and bonking them in the head works, but that's not reliable with 5 people. 

So, what advice is there? I can't duplicate Bernard to test fighting multiple people and previously managed this just fine, but this fight feels absolutely screwed.
